newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Ansett NZ triples annual profit, outlook positive.
newsitem.headline: Ansett NZ triples annual profit, outlook positive.

text.p: Airline Ansett New Zealand on Thursday reported a more than threefold increase in annual operating profit and said it was confident of sustaining further steady increases.
The airline, which competes domestically with Air New Zealand Ltd, said unaudited operating profits for the year to June 30 rose to NZ$9.05 million from $2.7 million.
Total revenues were up 4.2 percent at NZ$254 million.

Chief Executive Kevin Doddrell attributed the rise to cost control, better yield management practices and increased passenger volume. Customers exceeded two million for the first time in nine years of operation in New Zealand.
Passenger numbers on newly-introduced services to Hamilton in the North Island were three months ahead of budget target.
Doddrell cautioned that certain factors were likely to exert pressure on revenues and operating margins.

"We are mindful that the levelling off in growth of overseas visitor numbers, potential industrial action on the part of air traffic controllers and external environmental factors, such as the Mount Ruapehu (volcanic) eruptions, could all put pressure on our bottom line," he said.
The New Zealand air travel market would remain highly competitive.

Ansett would reinforce its operations in the coming year with expanded Christchurch workshop facilities and the introduction of a tenth BAe 146 Whisper Jet to the fleet. It would remain vigilant on cost control.
Air NZ said earlier this month it was investing A$475 million to buy TNT Ltd's half share in Ansett Airlines Investment Review Board.
News Ltd, which owns the other half of Ansett, will take full ownership of Ansett NZ to ensure the continuation of domestic competition in New Zealand.
New Zealand's anti-monopolies Commerce Commission had turned down an earlier version of the proposed Air NZ-Ansett deal because of concerns it would hurt domestic competition.
